label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: gas station tank
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (11 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 10 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- EPA has said one gallon of gasoline can make about a million gallons of groundwater unusable.
- Leaking underground storage tanks have been a leading source of groundwater contamination in America.
- New or replaced US underground tanks must have secondary containment (double walls) with interstitial monitoring
- US underground storage tanks must have spill prevention equipment such as a spill bucket at the fill pipe

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: the pit is dug, a steel tank appears and fills with amber gasoline. actions: dig dig (on "dig"); tank show (on "tank"); tank fuel (on "gasoline")
   idea: dig a pit, bury a steel tank and fill it with gasoline
   cue words: "dig", "tank", "gasoline"
2. problem
   on screen: drips fall from the tank and dark dots seep down through the soil. actions: drip start (on "rusts"); seep flow show (on "leaks"); soil leak seep1 (on "leaks"); soil leak seep2 (on "soil")
   idea: the steel rusts through and gasoline leaks into the soil
   cue words: "rusts", "leaks", "soil"
   its fact: Leaking underground storage tanks have been a leading source of groundwater contamination in America.
3. stakes
   on screen: the groundwater below turns murky. actions: soil leak murk (on "groundwater")
   idea: one gallon can ruin a million gallons of groundwater
   cue words: "groundwater", "million"
   its fact: EPA has said one gallon of gasoline can make about a million gallons of groundwater unusable.
4. fix1
   on screen: a green fiberglass second wall appears round the tank and the leak stops. actions: drip stop (on "So"); seep flow hide (on "So"); soil leak clear1 (on "wall"); soil leak clear2 (on "wall"); tank wrap (on "wall")
   idea: a second wall of fiberglass wraps the tank
   cue words: "So", "wall"
5. problem2
   on screen: amber fuel collects in the gap between the two walls. actions: tank seep (on "leak")
   idea: a leak into the gap between the walls stays hidden
   cue words: "leak"
6. fix2
   on screen: a sensor appears in the gap and its red light flashes. actions: tank sensor (on "sensor"); tank alarm (on "alarm")
   idea: a sensor in the gap flashes an alarm
   cue words: "sensor", "alarm"
   its fact: New or replaced US underground tanks must have secondary containment (double walls) with interstitial monitoring
7. problem3
   on screen: dark fuel runs from the sidewalk down beside the fill pipe. actions: tank alarmBack (on "But"); tank seepBack (on "But"); spill start (on "spills")
   idea: fuel spills at the fill pipe every time a delivery comes
   cue words: "But", "spills"
8. fix3
   on screen: a black spill bucket appears round the top of the fill pipe and the spill stops. actions: tank bucket (on "bucket"); spill stop (on "bucket")
   idea: a spill bucket round the fill pipe catches it
   cue words: "bucket"
   its fact: US underground storage tanks must have spill prevention equipment such as a spill bucket at the fill pipe
9. name
   on screen: an outline traces the tank. actions: tank outline show (on "underground")
   idea: this is an underground storage tank
   cue words: "underground"
10. finish
   on screen: a concrete cover slides over the pit and a fuel pump appears on it. actions: tank outline hide (on "Add"); cover grow (on "cover"); pump show (on "pump")
   idea: a concrete cover and a fuel pump on top
   cue words: "Add", "cover", "pump"
11. congrats
   on screen: a car pulls in beside the pump over the finished tank. actions: car arrive
   idea: you have built a gas station tank
   cue words: (none)
